Not long after this settlement Ailco died, and the following year the city, having bought the fortress of Minor Munta from its owners, again came to an agreement with Hissa, Ailco's widow, and likewise with his children, in this manner: The city leaves to Hissa and her children all those of their possessions which are rightly and without dispute theirs, until all the children, or some of them, reach a lawful age; then, according to the form of the compromise into which the city had entered with Ailco while he was alive, every dispute shall be settled for good, either by arbitrators or by judges; meanwhile the city keeps the fortress of Muntens together with one hundred acres from the two hundred, neither the best nor the worst, and all the jurisdiction attached to the fortress; complaints about mutual injuries or losses which occurred in the war are suspended for the time being. Sealed in the year 1440, in the month of November. So the city remained in possession of this, and in administration of justice throughout that whole neighbouring region, while the neighbours, who wished and sought it, grew weary of discord and of unequal jurisdiction, until the year 1460.

units.la: cccc. lx. Tum vero arbitris cum potestate lectis[?] hinc Theodorico Scaffero, Gofeno Gravio, inde Gerardo Petcumano, Egberto praefecto Em-dano, ita rursum pronunciatum. Hiffa cum liberis etiam reliqua illa centum jugera reci-peret, & cum caeteris rebus suis ac jurisdictio-nibus haberet, ijsq; uteretur frueretur: Groningani damna in aedificiis & rebus aliis ex aequo & bono ei repararent: arbitri definirent, an ijs quę retinerent, quęq; ex usufructu agrorum percepissent, satisfactum Groninganis pro injuriis esset. Nec quicquam amplius hac de re motum invenio ad annū usq; M. CCCC,
units.tr: 1460. Then indeed, with arbitrators chosen who had authority, namely Dietrich Schaffer and Gosen Grave on one side, and Gerhard Petkum and Egbert, prefect of Emden, on the other, the following judgement was again pronounced: Hissa, together with her children, should receive those remaining hundred acres as well, and should hold and enjoy them with her other property and jurisdictions; the Groningers should repair to her, in fairness and equity, the damage to buildings and other things; the arbitrators were to determine whether what she retained, and what she had gathered from the use of the lands, was sufficient satisfaction to the Groningers for their wrongs. I find nothing further moved on this matter until the year 1481.

units.la: LXXXI. Interim Eppone quoq; rebus humanis anno M. cccc. xliii aut M. cccc. xliiii exempto, qui in parte juris pristini, quod habere se à maioribus existimabat, in praefectura vetere remanserat, Groningani consensu populi, & pacto quodam cum Eppone freti, arcem eius Brocānum[?], deiecto praesidio, & vidua Epponis Frouwa Ulrici Grethani sorore) occuparunt, universumq; imperium pratorium secundum Dullarti oram in se verterunt, salvo reliquo jure, libertate, & ἀὐτονομία populi.
units.tr: 1481. Meanwhile Eppo too had departed from human affairs in the year 1443 or 1444; he had remained in the old district, claiming to hold a part of the ancient right which he thought he had from his ancestors. The Groningers, relying on the consent of the people and on a certain agreement with Eppo, drove out the garrison and seized his fortress at Brokum, with Eppo's widow Frouwa (sister of Ulrich Gretha) present; and they took into their own hands the whole praetorian rule along the shore of the Dollart, the rest of the right, liberty and autonomy of the people being left intact.

units.la: Datusq; à senatu praefectus, qui diceret jus, a quo provocatio ad senatum & civitatem esset. In eaq; conditione libens tota illa ora ad Dullartum sine mutatione ulla perstitit usq; ad tempora Saxonica, seq;[?] à repub. & societate reliquarum agri hujus partium se-junxit, nec exportandi importandive lege, nec cæteris pactis cum civitate obligata ab ea tempore fuit. Hoc exemplo vicini VVesterwol-[?]dij commoti, cum longius tendere, quam par esset, plusque juris, quam a majoribus relictum acceperat, usurpare EGGO ADDINGA agri Rector videretur, ad hæc violentius etiam quaedam ageret, injuriosius indigenas pariter & alios tractaret, judicata pro libidine aut exsequeretur, aut non exsequeretur, judicia eluderet, & ipsi quoque cum Groningensibus fœdus inierunt anno M. CCCC. XLVII: cujus fœderis itidem caput præcipuum fuit defensio libertatis: & cætera pene omnia ex formula ea, qua cum civitate hi, qui in vetere præfectura ad Dullar-tum sunt, anno M. CCCC. XXXV pepigerant.
units.tr: A prefect was appointed by the senate, who was to declare the law, from whom there would be an appeal to the senate and the city. Under this condition the whole of that shore along the Dollart remained willingly, without any change, until the Saxon times; and it separated itself from the commonwealth and alliance of the rest of this part of the land, and from the law of export and import, and from the other agreements, it was not bound to the city from that time. By this example the neighbours of Westerwolde, stirred up, when Eggo Adding, ruler of the land, seemed to stretch further than was fitting and to claim more right than he had received from his ancestors, and in addition acted more violently, treated natives and others alike more unjustly, either enforced or failed to enforce judgements as he pleased, and evaded the courts, themselves also entered into an alliance with the Groningers in the year 1447; the chief point of this alliance too was the defence of liberty, and almost everything else followed the form by which those who are in the old prefecture along the Dollart had agreed with the city in the year 1435.

units.la: Expresse vero cautum, si judices territorii (hi XII erant a populo & e populo electi) iniquè judicasse putarentur, liceret laeso senatum Groninganum appellare intra dies x; senatui jus esset, citare judices, & caussam recognoscere, & sententia tua vel appellantem temere, vel iniquè judicasse deprehensos in marcas veteres v condemnare: Atq; hæc omnia salvo Eggonis, & totius populi jure & libertate accepta a majoribus, quatenus hujus fœderis capitibus non adversantur. Fœdus vero esset perpetuum. Signatum pridie Bartholomæi.
units.tr: Expressly, however, it was provided that if the judges of the territory (there were twelve of them, chosen by the people and from the people) were thought to have judged unjustly, the injured party might appeal to the Senate of Groningen within ten days; the Senate would have the right to summon the judges and re-examine the case, and to condemn those found to have judged rashly or unjustly, whether the appellant or the judge, to five old marks: And all these things are to be done saving the right and liberty of Eggo and of the whole people, received from their ancestors, insofar as they do not conflict with the articles of this covenant. The covenant would be perpetual. Sealed the day before St Bartholomew's.

units.la: Eo fœdere ex hoc tempore usa civitas est, & eius metu repressus Eggo minus exorbitare ausus fuit, donec tandem proiecto metu, fœdereq; contempto, provecta iam ætate, Monasteriensium [?] patronorum fiducia insolentior fictus [?] ab iritata plebe est interemptus. Cuius mortem cum filius Haiyo ulciscereretur acerbius, ipsis crudelitatem improbantibus Monasteriensibus exorati a plebe Groningani, & propriis iniuriis quoq; lacessiti correptis armis eius arcem Weddana in potestate redactam aquarunt solo. Praetorium imperium, quod Haiyonis fuerat, sibi sumpsere summa plebis voluntate, praefectum, qui iurisdictioni praeesset, in arce Tekelburgia recens a se structa collocarunt. Et ne Monasterienses offenderent solutis xxv auri Rhenani libris eos deliniverunt, & jus, quod hactenus Eggo & Haiio velut beneficio eorum illic tenuerant, redemerunt. Additaq; pecunia data conditio, uti tantisper in possessione potestatis huiusce maneret civitas, donec pecunia ei esset restituta. Hoc modo exfoederatis Westerwoldiorum Rectores facti Groningani sunt, clientelam praesulis Monast. professi: duraruntq; in eo ad initia usq; Saxonici belli, quo cuncta in Frisia turbata. Quo eodem tempore, id quod inter Houverdaos & civitatem reliquum controversia erat, agitatum rursum, & arbitris demum commissum. Per eos confecta res quoquo modo primum inter Mennonem Omconemq; fratres, & civitatem: deinde post aliquot annos etiam inter Ailconem & Gerlachum Uphusanos, priorum fratris filios, ac eandem civitatem. Prioribus nescio qua re, posterioribus pecunia non ampla satisfactum: iurisdictio ab utrisq; civitati relicta.
units.tr: From this time the city used that covenant, and through fear of it Eggo, held in check, dared to go beyond his bounds less; until at last, having cast off his fear and despised the covenant, and now advanced in years, he grew more insolent through trust in the Münster patrons and was slain by the enraged common people. When his son Haiyo avenged his death more fiercely, the Münster men disapproved of the cruelty, but the people of Groningen, having been prevailed upon by the Münster men and also provoked by their own wrongs, took up arms and razed to the ground the citadel of Weddana, which had come into their power. They took for themselves the praetorial authority that had belonged to Haiyo, by the strong will of the common people, and placed a prefect, who was to preside over jurisdiction, in the citadel of Tekelburgia, recently built by them. And so that they should not offend the Münster men, they soothed them with twenty-five pounds of Rhenish gold, and bought back the right which Eggo and Haiyo had hitherto held there as a benefice from them. Money was added, and a condition given that the city should hold this power for as long as it remained in their possession until the money was repaid to them. In this way the men of Groningen became rulers of the Westerwolde, having abjured the covenant and professed the clientship of the Münster bishop; and they continued in this until the beginning of the Saxon war, by which all of Friesland was thrown into turmoil. At the same time, the dispute that remained between the Houverdas and the city was stirred up again and finally committed to arbiters. Through them the matter was settled, in some fashion, first between the brothers Mennon and Omcon and the city, and then after some years also between Ailcon and Gerlach of Uphusen, sons of the former brother, and the same city. The former were satisfied by I know not what means, the latter by no great sum of money; jurisdiction was relinquished to the city by both.

units.la: Sed redeo ad ea, unde sum, prolixius quam constitueram, digressus. Finitis foederibus ante memomemoratis, quæ cum reliquo agro inter Lavicam & Amafum civitas habebat, usus tamen eorum prorogatus tacito partium consensu, annoq; M. cccc. Lv. etiam de frumenti exportatione, & cerevisia scripto repetitum, & fancitum diligentius, ut in antigrapho quodam, quod apud ipsos agrarios est, legi. Denique cum pessum ire nonnulla, & diffluere sensim viderentur, & motus à CAROLO BVRGVNDO ingrueret Frisia minitante, optimi & prudentissimi quiq; reipub. & patriæ totius cura tacti id effecere studio suo, ut proluxius accuratius quam unquam prius civitati cum Fivelgonys, Hunesgonys, Meda-chys, Langowoldys, Fredowoldys, Hummercys solenni modo fœdus sit instauratum, cum fluere annuum à natali Servatoris nostri M. cccc. LXXXIII.
units.tr: But I return to what I was discussing, having digressed at greater length than I intended. When the covenants mentioned above, which the city had with the rest of the land between Lavica and Amasus, had ended, their use was nevertheless extended by the tacit consent of the parties; and in the year 1455 concerning the export of grain and beer it was renewed in writing and confirmed more carefully, as can be read in a certain copy which is kept among the land-men themselves. Finally, when some things seemed to be going to ruin and gradually to be dissolving, and the movement of Charles of Burgundy, threatening Friesland, was bearing down, the best and wisest men of each commonwealth, moved by care for the state and for the whole fatherland, took care with their zeal that the covenant should be renewed in the solemn manner, more fully and more carefully than ever before, between the city and the Fivelgo, Hunsego, Medacha, Langewold, Fredewold and Hummercha, the year then running from the birth of our Saviour 1483.
In it these were the chief provisions:

units.la: Vt pacatè inter se viverent omnes, auxilio sibi mutuò essent contra quoslibet hostes, maximè libertati imminentes, contraq; eos, qui domi judiciis & legibus non parerent: vis omnis & tumultus statim comprimeretur; conventus juridici superiores GRONINGÆ agerentur quater quotannis aut sæpius, quibus HOVETMANNI oppidani præsidè-rent, ad quos provocatio esset à tribunalibus omnibus in agro. Conventus hos Hovetmanni cum judicibus aliis indicerent: quod frumenti in agro provenit, id non exportaretur, nec alibi quam in urbe venum proponeretur: in tabernis & diversoriis non alius q Groninganæ cerevisiæ esset usus: Nec cuiquam per totum agrum vendendi, ac quæstus faciendi causa cerevisiam coquere liceret : fœdus hoc decennium proximum valeret.
units.tr: That all should live peacefully among themselves, should assist one another against any enemies whatever, especially those threatening liberty, and against those who at home would not submit to judgments and laws: all violence and disturbance would be suppressed at once; superior judicial assemblies would be held at Groningen four times a year or more often, presided over by the townsmen called Hovetmanni, to whom appeal would lie from all the tribunals in the land. The Hovetmanni, together with the other judges, would appoint these assemblies. As to grain grown in the land, it was not to be exported, nor offered for sale anywhere but in the city; in taverns and inns only Groningen beer was to be used; nor was anyone to be allowed to brew beer throughout the whole land for the purpose of selling it and making profit; this covenant was to hold good for the next ten years.
Sealed the 6th day of August.

units.la: Eodem anno, crescente, quem dixi, ab armis Burgundicis metu, cum fœdus cum Tranflavi-canis confici ob simultates atq; odia intestina non posset, cum THEDA & Frisii orientalibus fo-cietas à civitate ordinibusq; agrarijs inita est pro tuenda libertate certe memorabilis: de qua in historia scripsi plenius. Mox alio se ver-tente Burgundo, legati à civitate, & socijs vicinis missi ad Cæsarem FRIDERICVM III, qui & libertatis pristinæ, & pactorum recentium confirmationem, patrocinium contra Burgundum peterent. Impetratum, de libertate, pactaq; firmata, tota regio denique in tutelam recepta imperij. Sed ex ea legatione non magnam gratiam, honoremve Joannes Rengerus, & Unico Ripperda retulere, qui pro repub. missi sua potius quam reip. agen-tes potestatem peramplam iuris dicundi, exigendi vectigalis, cudendæ aureæ monetæ (hanc civitas pro se petierat) & nescio qua alia sibi acquisivere: quamquam prohibiti ab ordinibus patriæ uti beneficio Cæsaris non potuerint. Simul tota regio durante hoc fœdere in summa quiete & felicitate egit, civitas divitijs, operibus novis, magnificentia, amplitudine, ager cultu & nitore crevit, ac fuit summa inter socios animorum & gerendæ reip.coniunctio. Hoc tempore, casu iam ad Nanceium Carolo Burgundo, Arnoldus Lovs iureconsultus à Cæsare Friderico ad componendas res per Frisiam Transflavicanam missus consilij capiendi causa Groningam deflexit. Eo autore civitas in spem venit perpetuæ potestatis jus in agrum vicinum sibi parandi: paravisset, & alia quoq; adiecisset, quantum in Cæsare erat, si pecunia dispendium in loco facere[?] moluisset.
units.tr: In that same year, with the fear of the Burgundian arms growing, as I have said, and since a covenant could not be made with the Trans-Lauwers men because of private feuds and internal hatreds, an alliance was entered into by the city and the land-orders with Theda and the eastern Frisians for defending liberty, certainly a memorable one; I have written about it more fully in my history. Soon, Burgundy turning elsewhere, envoys were sent by the city and the neighbouring allies to Emperor Frederick III, to seek his protection against Burgundy and the confirmation of their former liberty and recent pacts. This was obtained: their liberty and pacts were confirmed, and the whole region was finally taken into the protection of the Empire. But from that embassy John Rengers and Unico Ripperda brought back no great favour or honour; sent on behalf of the commonwealth, yet acting more for themselves than for the commonwealth, they acquired for themselves very ample power of administering justice, of collecting tolls, of minting gold coin (this the city had requested for itself), and I know not what else; although, forbidden by the orders of the land, they could not make use of the Emperor's favour. At the same time, while this covenant lasted, the whole region lived in the greatest quiet and prosperity: the city grew in wealth, new buildings, magnificence and extent, and the land in cultivation and finery, and there was the greatest unity of minds and of government among the allies. At this time, by chance, Charles of Burgundy being already at Nancy, Arnold Lovs, a jurist sent by Emperor Frederick to settle affairs throughout Trans-Lauwers Friesland, turned aside to Groningen to take counsel. Through his guidance the city came to hope for a perpetual right to acquire power over the neighbouring land for itself: it would have acquired it, and would have added other things too, as far as lay with the Emperor, had it been unwilling to spend money on the matter in the place.

units.la: Rediit enim Lovs denuò à Cæsare, amplissimis in hanc rem mandatis instructus. Sed illa aulæ cupidine offensa, post posito consilio hoc, ina-nem legatum remisit. Et jam ad exitum pene properabat tempus, quod erat fœderi dictum, ut aut prorogato eodem, aut novato ampliatove opus esse videretur. Gaudebat quippe utraq; pars fœdere, eiusq; fructu suaviter afficiebatur. Itaq; data utrimq; opera est, ut ampliarum[?] rebus & tempore denuo feriretur. Idq; confectum exeunte anno M. CCCC. LXXXII, triduo ante natalem domini: tempus et decretum superiore maius. Eius capita præcipua fuere hæc, ut sunt in historia à me expressa. Pax inter partes esset, salvo cuiq; legitimo jure suo; auxiliis se mutuò juvarent, si res auxiliis egeret; temerè nemo in exilium pelleretur, nisi criminum gravium reus, & contumax: ex legibus sese mutuò convenirent, omni vi missa: principes externos, & quoscunq; alios vim sociis afferentes, aut libertatem prementes communi operâ pro viribus arcerent: postulati auxilia ferrent ad arbitrium bonorum virorum & statim,& suis sumptibus,cessantesque in hoc officio M.icu-tatos veteres in usum apparatus bellici pen-derent: tumultuantes comprimerentur ma-turé:si qui turbata pace publica ceperint alios, ac fpoliarint, captos dimitterent confestim, spolioque dupliciter reftituro insuper gravem multam fœderi luerent: fine consensu com-muni bellum nemo moveret: in auxilium evocati à sociis fidei firmandæ causa obsides traderent Groningæ custodiendos usque ad expeditionis finem. Tum, de judicijs sic. Iudicibus in agro aut jus reddere detrectanti-bus, aut petperam judicantibus, jus effet læso appellare tribunal superius, in quo judicant omnes totius societatis ordines legitimé convocati, ejusque appellationis testimonium scriptum petere GRONINGÆ intra diem x. quo accepto, non liceret judici inferiori quicquam in eum porro decernere,aut contra eum agere, aut repetenti pignora, fi qua sint ablata,ac sponsionem præstare volenti in mo-ra aut impedimento esse: aut illum diem fi negligeret læsus, omnino judicato priori pa-reret: appellans causam suam persequeretur tribus proximis in conventibus judicialibus in ipsa urbe,aut marcas penderet veteres quinque mulctæ nomine, insuperque causa sua caderet: atque hic effet litium trahendarum terminus, nec fas esset in hoc quicquam mutare, nisi ex mutuo litigantium partium consensu: judex inferior, à cujus judicio provocatum esset, fi non veniret ipse tuendæ sententiæ suæ gratia ad conventum, primum detrimento id non esset appellanti, deinde præter emansitationis pœnam vsitatam, quinquë etiam marcas fisco solveret: si latam ab eo sententiam confirmari contingeret, potesta-tem haberet totam causam porrò definiendi, etiam si anno suo evoluto magistratu jam ab-ijsset: ad conventum judicialem coëuntibus judicandi gratiâ quantumvis raro numero jus esset ac potestas causas definiendi, non secus ac si frequentes convenirent: Conven-tus hujusmodi Groningæ agerentur quotan-nis quater aut sæpius, si reip. ratio, id videtur poscere: essetq; in eo, vt & in tempore conventuum designando, arbitrium prætorum ab oppidanis datorum (HOVETMAN-NOS vocant) & eorum qui res per agrum in tribunalibus inferioribus judicant: Deinde de sontium pœnis aut mulctis hæc. Furti, latrocinij, proditionis, incendiorum reos recep-tare fas non esset, aut pœnis eripere: pœna omnium horum supplicium capitis. Cædes cujusvis hominis in conventu publico præ-sentis, aut istuc euntis, aut redeuntis ab eo, mulctâ lueretur sexcuplâ: idem juris de vul-nere, aliáve injuria esset; consulis verò aut se-natoris, aut viri nobilis, aut judicis, aut sacer-dotis cædes, vulnus, injuria mulctâ corripe-tur duodecuplâ: ejus mulctæ triens ærario, bes læso, aut propinquis ejus cederet: si reus solvendo non esset, sex propinqui proximi læso, aut læsi propinquis pro ipso satisface-rent, aut reum saltem ijsdem sisterent: omnes deniq; injuriæ ubicunq; & quocunq; tempore patratæ hoc duranre fœdere in triplum puni-retur supra modum in legibus patriis defi-nitum, nitum: salvo interea unicuiq; jure suo, ac pactis mutuis, quæ hisce non adversarentur. Demum & ista addita, quæ ad civitatis commodum pertinent. Frumenti in agro sociorum nati exportatio non effet in regiones alias:
units.tr: For Lovs returned again from the Emperor, furnished with the fullest instructions for this business. But the court, offended by his eagerness, after dropping this plan, sent back the envoy with nothing done. And now the time that had been set for the covenant was nearly running out, so that it seemed necessary either to extend the same or to renew and enlarge it. Indeed each party rejoiced in the covenant and was pleasantly affected by its fruits. Therefore efforts were made on both sides that the matter might be struck again, with enlargements, and at the time. And this was concluded at the end of the year 1482, three days before the Lord's birth: the time and decree greater than before. Its chief heads were these, as I have set them out in my history. There was to be peace between the parties, each person's lawful right being saved; they were to help one another with aid if the situation needed aid; no one was to be lightly driven into exile, unless he were guilty of grave crimes and contumacious; they were to come together by the laws, all violence being put aside; foreign princes, and whoever else brought violence upon the allies or oppressed their liberty, were to be kept off by common effort according to their strength; those requested were to bring aid at the judgment of good men, and immediately and at their own expense, and those who were slack in this duty were to pay ten old marks for the use of the war-equipment; rioters were to be quickly restrained; if anyone, having disturbed the public peace, had seized others and plundered them, he was to release the captives at once, and in addition pay a heavy fine to the covenant, restoring the plunder twofold; no one was to begin war without common consent; those summoned to aid by the allies were to hand over hostages, to be kept at Groningen until the end of the expedition, for the sake of confirming the alliance. Then, concerning judicial matters, it was as follows. If judges in the land either refused to render justice or judged perversely, the injured party was to have the right to appeal to a higher tribunal, in which the lawfully summoned orders of the whole alliance sit in judgment, and to seek at Groningen, within ten days, a written testimony of that appeal. On receiving it, no lower judge was to decree anything further against him, or act against him, or obstruct or hinder him who sought the return of pledges, if any had been taken away, or who wished to give security; or if the injured party neglected that day, he was altogether to obey the earlier judgment. The appellant was to pursue his cause at the three nearest judicial assemblies in the city itself, or else pay five old marks as a fine, and in addition lose his cause; and this was to be the limit of protracting lawsuits, and it was not right to change anything in this, except by mutual consent of the litigating parties. A lower judge, from whose judgment an appeal had been made, if he did not come himself to the assembly to defend his sentence, would first not suffer loss on this account to the appellant, and then, besides the customary penalty of contumacy, would also pay five marks to the treasury; if it happened that the sentence he had given was confirmed, he would have the power of finally deciding the whole case, even if, his year of office having run out, he had already left his post; to the judicial assembly, those gathering for the purpose of judging, however small their number, were to have the right and power of deciding cases, just as if they had gathered in full numbers. Assemblies of this kind were to be held at Groningen four times a year or more often, if the state of the commonwealth seemed to require it; and in this, both in appointing the times of the assemblies, the decision was to lie with the Hovetmanni chosen by the townsmen and with those who judge matters in the lower tribunals throughout the land. Next, concerning the penalties or fines for offenders, these provisions: it was not lawful to harbour or to snatch from punishment those accused of theft, robbery, treason or arson; the penalty for all these was the death penalty. Killing any man whatever present at a public assembly, or going to it or returning from it, was to be atoned for with a sixfold fine; the same law applied to wounding or other injury; but the killing, wounding or injury of a consul, senator, noble, judge or priest was to be punished with a twelvefold fine, a third of which would go to the treasury, and the rest to the injured party or his kin; if the guilty party were unable to pay, six nearest kinsmen of the injured party, or of the injured person's kin, were to stand surety for him, or at least produce the accused before them. Finally, all injuries committed anywhere and at any time while this covenant lasted were to be punished threefold beyond the measure defined in the laws of the fatherland; saving meanwhile to each his own right, and the mutual agreements which were not opposed to these. Lastly these also were added, which pertain to the advantage of the city. The export of grain born in the land of the allies was not to go to other regions;

units.la: Cerevisiam in tabernis vendere, aut in usu habere exoticam rota in regione non liceret, nisi quantum antiftibus aut nobilibus aut cæteris viris honestis condere ejus in penuaria sua in usum domesticum liberet: nec coquere etiam toto in agro cerevisiam distrahendi causa cuiquam extra urbem permissum: sed qui vellet, coqueret tantum, quantum fatis effet familiæ suæ: veniret autem solum ea, quæ a civibus in urbe coacta. Postremo sub exitum fœderis utri parti conditio ejus displiceret, nec liberet ea uti diutius, toto anno ante exitum ejus renunciaret eidem folenniter. Hoc fœdus quamdiu stetit & cultum fine vitio est, florentif-sima res urbis & agri fuere, adeò ut inuidiam meruisse ex fortuna videantur. Tum-structa in urbe est turris illa maximi operis & impendij, vasta molis & forma superba ex saxo Bonthe-mio, templo [?]Martiniano adsidens, tum adifica-tum magnificum oenopolium in-fori medio, tum ædes privatæ complures sumptu ingenti erectæ, negociationes etiam aulæ plurimum, & opes publicæ privataq;, multiplicatæ, deniq; boe[?] fortuna vivo elata civitas, ut commeatuum haberet copiam liberiorum & ampliores,re cum[?] episcopo [?]Monasteriensi, Emdensium rebus mi-nico, comparata, [?]Amafi aluum[?] alio divertere, & in Dullarti sinus superiora, qua ipsa impe-rium habet, derivare est conata, quanquam co-natu frustraneo, & oleo operaque in eo perdita:postremo trans Lavicam fidentius tentare res, &imperium proferre ausa fiat. De quo nunc di-cere, & conjunctionem civitatis cum Transla-vicanis paulo altius repetere, ut res clarius eluce-scat, ordo & tempus monent.
units.tr: To sell beer in the taverns, or to keep foreign beer in use in the region, would not be permitted, except that the bishops, the nobles and other respectable men might store as much of it in their cellars as they wished for domestic use. Nor was anyone outside the city allowed to brew beer throughout the whole countryside for the purpose of selling it. Whoever wished could brew only as much as was enough for his own household; and only beer brewed by the citizens within the city might be brought to market. Finally, toward the end of the covenant, if either party was dissatisfied with its terms and did not wish to keep using it any longer, it was to notify the other party formally a full year before its expiry. As long as this covenant stood and was kept without fault, the city and the countryside were most prosperous, so much so that they seem to have earned envy from fortune. Then in the city was built that tower of very great labour and expense, of vast bulk and proud form, made of Bentheim stone and standing beside the church of St Martin; then a magnificent wine-house was built in the middle of the market; then several private houses were erected at great cost; and trade too, and the public and private wealth, greatly multiplied, and finally the city, elated by its fortune, grew so that it had a greater and freer supply of provisions, having been acquired with the bishop of Münster in the affairs of the Emden people, who were diminished. They tried to divert the Ems elsewhere and to lead the upper reaches of the Dollart inlet, where the province itself holds sway, but the attempt failed, and effort and labour were lost in it. Lastly, the city boldly ventured to try its fortunes more confidently across the Lauwers and to extend its rule. Of this matter, now to speak, and to trace back somewhat further the union of the city with the Translavicans, so that the matter may be made clearer, order and time advise.
On the Union of the State with the Translavicans.

units.la: IN Translavicanis Octopagici, Cislavicanis finitimi, primi post Scingios à Kenone Groninga eiectos, commodo societatis cum civitate animadverso, isdem conditionibus, quibus Hummercij, Langowoldij, Fredowoldij in commune fœdus ascripti, eidem quoq; se potestati praetoriæ subiecere, & eadem, quæ inde profluunt commoda civitati tribuerunt, cum annus sueret à nato Christo M. cccc. xvi: tempusq; fœderi dederunt decennium. Deinde finito decennio, cum utilitatem rei essent experti, metuerentq; priora mala tφόροις demptis, fœdus idem indefinite, nullo statuto termino prorogarunt, additis etiam ad priores socios Hunefgonijs & Fivelgonijs,sed con-ventuum loco eAdoardiæ[?] constituto. Hinc post annos XVIII, anno scil. M. CCCC. XLIV, Ostbroecsterani,Collumani,Suachi[?],Olduvoldi, Gastÿ[?] pasti cum civitate Groningana sunt in hanc sententiam: Si iudices ipsorum in coër-cendis maleficiis officium non facerent, jus ef-set senatui urbano, & hovetmannis, mandare iis, ut facerent: Si ne tum quidem moveri[?] se sinerent, citaretur ab iisdem GRONINGAM ad conventum juridicum: & causa cognita, si cefsase in officio deprehenderentur, multam gravem poscerentur, & ad solvendam eam compellerentur. Nec multis interiectis die-bus omnes OSTERGOI, ut se domesticis turbis ac dissensionibus perpetuis liberarent, cum frustra id prius pactionibus inter se, & cum Westergois vicinis quaesissent[?] propter factionum[?] pertinaciam sepe pacta perrumpentem, ad huius eiusdem civitatis Groningana societatem confugerunt, conventumq; juridicum ad cognoscendas controversias majores, de quibus provocatum ab XVIII viris judicibus superioribus, curandaq; negocia reip. agendum semel quotannis GRONINGAE collocarunt. Ad hæc statuerunt, ut in arbitriis rerum criminalium, si arbitri convenire non possent, SENATVS GRO-NINGANVS summus arbiter fieret; atque interim reus obsides solvendi judicati eidem daret; ut item nobilis vir nobilem occidens, luendæ pœnæ cccc marcarum veterum intra annum vertentem obsides Groningæ deponeret, atq; insuper Groninganæ reip. marcas similes xx, totidemq; singulis Oftergoæ partibus pro multa penderet: eo facto, extra periculum esset: si non daret obsides, atq; interea aliquid à propinquis occisi paterétur, id autoribus esset impune. Deniq; sic recepere Oftergoi, operam daturos se coniunctis studijs, ut VVESTERGOI quoq; eidem fœderi ijsdem conditionibus accederent. Hoc fœdus valeret quadriennium. Sed prorogatum duravit diutius ad adventum ufq; Thoma Gurt-stedij legati Cæsaris, qui in Frisiam venit anno M. CCCC. LVI. & ni me animus fallit, etiam ulterius. Nam eo tempore quæsita apud imperatorem antiquatio eius est à Weftergois & Scringys[?]: at antiquatum esse nominatim in diplomatis tunc impetratis non invenio.
units.tr: The Translavicans of the Eight Districts, neighbours of the Cislavicans, were the first, after the Scingi were expelled from Groningen by Kenno, to notice the advantage of alliance with the city. On the same terms by which the Hummerges, the Langwolders and the Fredewolders had been enrolled in the common league, they also submitted themselves to the praetorian authority of the city and granted the city the same benefits that flow from it. This happened in the year from the birth of Christ 1416, and they gave the league a term of ten years. Then, when the ten years were over, having found the advantage of the arrangement, and fearing their former troubles now that the tributes had been removed, they extended the same league indefinitely, without fixing any end, adding also to the earlier allies the Hunsingoers and the Fivelgoers, though the place of the assemblies was set at Leeuwarden. Hence, eighteen years later, in the year 1444, the men of Oostbroek, Collum, Suawoud[?], Olduvoldi and Gasty[?] made a pact with the city of Groningen to this effect: if their judges did not perform their duty in punishing crimes, the city council and the hoofdelingen would have the right to order them to do so; if even then they allowed themselves to be left unmoved, they would be summoned by the same men to Groningen before the judicial assembly, and, once the case was heard, if they were found to have failed in their duty, they would be fined heavily and compelled to pay it. Not many days later all the Ostergoers, so that they might free themselves from their domestic disorders and constant dissensions, which they had first sought in vain to remedy by agreements among themselves and with their neighbours the Westergoers, because of the obstinacy of the factions which often broke the pacts, took refuge in the alliance with this same city of Groningen. They established a judicial assembly in Groningen, to hear the greater controversies, which were appealed from the eighteen superior judges, and to transact the business of the commonwealth once a year. In addition they decided that in arbitrations concerning criminal matters, if the arbiters could not agree, the city council of Groningen should become the supreme arbiter; and meanwhile the accused should give to that council hostages for payment of the judgment. Likewise, a nobleman who killed a nobleman should, to pay the penalty of 400 old marks within a year, deposit hostages at Groningen, and in addition pay as a fine twenty similar marks to the commonwealth of Groningen and as many to each part of Ostergo; once this was done he would be out of danger; if he did not give hostages and in the meantime suffered something at the hands of the relatives of the slain man, this would be unpunished for those who had done it. Finally the Ostergoers thus undertook to labour, with united efforts, that the Westergoers too should join this league on the same terms. This league was to hold for four years. But it was extended and lasted longer, until the arrival of Thomas Gurtstede, envoy of the Emperor, who came to Friesland in the year 1456, and, if my mind does not deceive me, even longer. For at that time the Westergoers and the Scringi sought from the Emperor its annulment; but I do not find that it was named as annulled in the documents then obtained.

units.la: Similiter vero & SMALINGANI anno, qui proxime pactionem hanc Oftergoorum secutus fuit, aliquid huius generis cum ijsdem oppidanis, & eorum sociis vicinis pepigere. Imprimis hic cautum, ut judiciales conventus agerentur quotannis, indicente senatu Groningano: & si socij hi novi suo in agro conventum haberi cuperent, ut hoc senatui significasent; is porrò edicto suo socios convocaret.
units.tr: Likewise, in the year that most closely followed this pact of the Ostergoers, the Smallingers also made some agreement of this kind with the same townsmen and with their neighbouring allies. Chiefly it was provided here that judicial assemblies should be held every year, summoned by the city council of Groningen; and if these new allies wished an assembly to be held in their own district, they were to signify this to the council, which would then summon the allies by its edict.

units.la: Anno deinceps M. CCCC- LXI VPSTERANI, qui etiam sunt ad occidentem Lavica amnis, eandem secuti causam, ut dissensionibus intestinis & periculis se eximerent, ad idem quoq; remedium rursum convolarunt. Nam inflaurata memoria & vi veteris fœderis, nouum multis capitibus autem cum senatu populoq; Groningano percus-serunt. ferunt in perpetuum. In eo hæc sunt.
units.tr: In the year 1461 afterwards, the Upstreamers, who also dwell on the western side of the river Lauwers, pursuing the same cause, so that they might free themselves from intestine dissensions and dangers, again flocked together to the same remedy. For, having renewed the memory and force of the old league, they struck a new one with the council and people of Groningen, in many chapters. They carry it in perpetuity. Its contents are these.

units.la: HOVETMANNI Groningani, adhibitis incon-filium tribus aut quatuor Vpfteranis homi-nibus honestis, prætorem toti agro creanto quotannis die translationis S. Martini, & similiter judices binos in parochiis majoribus, singulos in minoribus ex ordine eorum omnes, qui propria prædia in agro Vpfterano possident: hi jus omnibus æqualiter dicunto ex legibus patriis. Si in eo negligent, aut facere non volent officium suum, HOVETMANNI Groningani compellantor, ijque sub pœna primum scutatorum x, deinde xx, postremò contumaciæ mandanto, vt jus petentibus ex-pediant: mulctaque huiusmodi ex semisse civitatis, reliquum reip. Vpfteranæ esto. Electus prætor aut judex munus annuum non recusato, aut x scutatos reipub. pendito. Prætor judicesque sententiam à fe latam petentibus scriptam exhibento. Ad hac appellandi ius esto, fi quis volet, ad HOVETMANNOS Groninganos intra diem decimum. Quo rité facto, prior judex non procedito longius: causa refertor ad conventum iuredi-cialem proximum in vrbe. Appellans verò fi non persequetur litem in proximo, aut sal-lem altero conventu, non solum lite cadito, sed etiam marcas quinque multam solvito, nisi forte iudex, qui sententiam tulit, ad conventum ipse non veniat: hoc enim appellantem à pœna absolvet, iudex verò emanfitans pœnam pendito. Idem iudex & appellans quinas marcas deponunto apud conventum, amittitoq; depositum, qui succumbet,victor recipito. Signatum fœdus feria quarta a pentecostes anno M. CCCC. LXI.
units.tr: The hoofdelingen of Groningen, with the advice of three or four honourable men of the Upstreamers, shall appoint each year, on the day of the translation of St Martin, a praetor for the whole district, and likewise two judges in the larger parishes and one each in the smaller, from the whole body of those who possess their own estates in the Upstream district; these shall dispense justice equally to all according to the ancestral laws. If they are negligent in this, or are unwilling to perform their duty, the hoofdelingen of Groningen shall compel them, under penalty first of ten gold shields, then of twenty, and finally they shall be ordered, as a mark of contumacy, to provide justice to those seeking it; and a fine of this kind shall be half for the city and the rest for the commonwealth of the Upstreamers. The elected praetor or judge shall not refuse the office for the year, or else shall pay ten gold shields to the commonwealth. The praetor and the judges shall exhibit in writing to those seeking it the sentence pronounced by them. In addition there shall be the right of appeal, if anyone wishes, to the hoofdelingen of Groningen within ten days. If this is properly done, the earlier judge shall proceed no further; the case shall be referred to the next judicial assembly in the city. But if the appellant does not pursue the suit at the next assembly, or at least at the second, he shall not only lose the suit but also pay a fine of five marks, unless perhaps the judge who pronounced the sentence does not himself come to the assembly; for this will absolve the appellant from the penalty, while the judge who fails to appear shall pay the penalty. The same judge and the appellant shall deposit five marks each with the assembly, and the one who loses shall forfeit his deposit, and the winner shall recover it. The league was signed on the Wednesday after Pentecost in the year 1461.

units.la: Sexennio post CoLLVMANI quoq; eorumq; vi-cini seditionibus agitati diu, ac misere afflicti, nec aliud remedium ullum conspicati, multis & exquisitis precibus fatigaruut Groninganos, vt se in-fœdus reciperent. Assensu impetrato, fœdus initum in annos xxx. Eius hac fuit sententia.
units.tr: Six years later the people of Collum too, and their neighbours, long troubled by seditions and miserably afflicted, and seeing no other remedy, with many and urgent prayers wearied the Groningers, that they might be received into the league. Their assent being obtained, a league was entered into for thirty years. Its purport was this.

units.la: Civitas & Collumani, cæterisq; interfecom-[?]parent de domo valida & idonea, in qua, ut in arce, sedem habeat præfectus a civitate dandus in annos proximos vi. In huius præfecti stipendium quotannis pecunia confera-tur viritim per totum agrum, ab aliis scutatus aureus, ab aliis semissis[?], pensionibus duabus: Ipse auxilio sit omnibus contra vim ac iniuriam: valla, fossas, cætera munitionum poscente præfecto populus perficiat: post sexennium civitas & socii dispiciat, præsidiône diutius fit opus, & quod videbitur iis, id valeat: criminum iudicia exerceantur ex legibus proximo seculo Groningæ recognitis: nemo factionibus tumultibusve aliis etiam extra regionem se misceat, aut suos miscere se sinat: contra vim armatam socij sibi multuo auxilio sint: Turbatę pacis gravis multa fit aureorum scutatorum mille, aut pœna capitis, si quis multam solvere non queat: vis omnis absit, non armis, sed judicio controversiæ disceptentur, facinora severe reprimantur: æris alieni solutio expediatur: in controversiis civilibus appellatio fit ad judices urbanos, quemadmodū recepreceptum apud alios, qui cum civitate fœdus habent: qui in legationem ad senatum non consensere per agrum Collumanum & vicinum, in quibus ij, qui sunt prius nominati, fœdere hoc non sint comprehensi: fœdus valeat in annos xxx. Signatum anno M. CCCC. LXVII postridie Nonarum Septembr. Prefecti duo, quod id expedire in initio videretur, in agrum Collumanum missi, Hillebrandus Brandus, & Sibrandus Ulferdi. Ita quies ibi parta: anno postero domus praefecto structa. Post hæc cum dissidia & turbæ crebresscerent rursus in Ostergoa, flammaq, ea Westergoa quoq, afflaretur, scintillaretq, passim studium factionum, & cum civitate Groningana multorum simultas ex invidia & metu glisceret, ne quid inde maioris existeret mali, tandem anno M. CCCC. LXXVII, prudentum & bonorum studio, omnis VVESTERGOA & OSTERGOA in fœdus decenne cum civitate Groningana consensit: cuius hæc summa. Id quod anno M. cccc. XXII, à tota gente Frifica Groningæ initum fœdus fuit, ratum fit, salvo nupero fœdere Collumano; Groninganis non liceat hoc decennio ullam præterea Ostergoæ aut VVestergoæ partem fœdere huiusmodi implicare, aut prætoriæ potestati suæ subijcere; Conventus quotannis agatur alternis vicibus Groningæ & Leoardiæ, ad quem quini ab vtraq; parte homines sapientes mittantur: his x. vndecimus adiiciatur, quem ex Ostergoa aut VVestergoa quini Groningani eligent, cum conventus agetur Leoardiæ: quini vero Tranflavicani, ex oppido aut agro Groningarro[?], cum conventus ille Groningæ habebitur. Horum arbitrij sit causas omnes publicas & privatas, quæ in controuersiam venient, cognoscere, disceptare, definire: quicquid definiuerint, ab omnib. ratum habeatur: intraq; præfixum tempus executioni mandetur ab ijs apud quos sedes tenet condemnatus, aut ab ipsis illis multa petatur: contumaces, si qui erunt, coniunctis viribus ad parendum compellantur. Eorundem deleCtorum potestatis quoq; sit, si id ex usu reip. esse putabunt, alterum conventus diem in Smallingeraeo cœnobio dicere. Ad eum ituris, domumq; redituris tutus commeatus præstetur: Quod si finito decennio hoc non placuerit hæc pacta prorogare, aut nova alia inire, fœdera tamen superiora & pax nihilominus rata serventur.
units.tr: The state and the men of Collum and the other ... shall provide a strong and suitable house, in which, as in a citadel, the prefect to be given by the state for the next six years shall have his seat. For the prefect's salary a sum shall be contributed every year, per head, throughout the whole district: from some a gold shield, from others a half, in two instalments. He himself shall be a help to all against violence and injury; the people shall complete the walls, ditches and other fortifications, as the prefect demands. After six years the state and the allies shall consider whether a garrison is needed longer, and whatever seems good to them shall hold. Judgments in criminal matters shall be carried out according to the laws recently revised at Groningen. No one shall mix himself in factions, tumults or other disturbances, even outside the region, nor allow his people to mix themselves in them. Against armed violence the allies shall give mutual help with all their strength. For disturbance of the peace the fine shall be a heavy one of a thousand gold shields, or the penalty of death if someone cannot pay the fine. All violence shall cease; disputes shall be settled not by arms but by judgment; crimes shall be severely repressed; the payment of debts shall be arranged. In civil controversies appeal shall be made to the city judges, as has been received among the others who have a league with the state. Those who did not consent to the embassy to the council are not included in this league throughout the district and neighbourhood of Collum, in which the persons named first are not comprehended. The league shall hold for thirty years. Signed in the year 1467, the day after the Nones of September. Two prefects, since it seemed expedient at the outset, were sent into the district of Collum: Hillebrand Brand and Sibrand Ulferd. Thus quiet was secured there; in the following year a house was built for the prefect. After this, when dissensions and disturbances grew more frequent again in Ostergo, and the flame was also fanned in Westergo, and the spirit of faction was kindled everywhere, and the enmity of many against the city of Groningen grew from envy and fear, lest some greater evil should arise from this, at last in the year 1477, by the zeal of the prudent and good, the whole of Westergo and Ostergo agreed to a league of ten years with the city of Groningen. Its substance was this. That the league made at Groningen in the year 1422 by the whole Frisian people is ratified, saving the recent league of Collum. For these ten years the Groningers shall not be permitted to involve any other part of Ostergo or Westergo in a league of this kind, or to subject it to their praetorian authority. Assemblies shall be held every year, alternately at Groningen and at Leeuwarden, to which five wise men from each side shall be sent. To these an eleventh shall be added, whom the five Groningers shall choose from Ostergo or Westergo when the assembly is held at Leeuwarden; and the five Translavicans, from the town or district of Groningen, when that assembly is held at Groningen. It shall be the duty of these men to hear, dispute and decide all public and private causes that come into controversy; whatever they have decided shall be held valid by all; and within a fixed time it shall be carried out by those in whose district the condemned man resides, or the fine shall be demanded from them; the contumacious, if there are any, shall be compelled by united force to obey. It shall also be within the power of these same chosen men, if they think it is for the good of the commonwealth, to appoint another day of assembly in the monastery of Smallingerland. For those going to it and returning home, safe passage shall be granted. But if at the end of the decade it is not pleasing to extend these agreements or to enter into other new ones, the earlier leagues and the peace shall nevertheless be kept in force.

units.la: Anno ab hoc altero, qui fuit M. CCCC. LXXIX, ARNOL-DUS Lovs, quem dixi, ab imperatore legatus in Frisiam venit cum ampla potestate, & re infecta ob quam venerat, discessurus Groninganos sibi substituit, procurandam regionem inter Lavicam & Flevum ipsis commendavit: simul promisit, si ad hanc rem ampliore mandato & literis a Cæsare se opus habere putarent, ista sese confecturum, transmissurumq; quam primum, idq; sine sollicitatione ac monito ipsorum, sponte & studio suo: jussitq; pro ea, quam habebat potestate, ut delegatum minus & curam serio, & cum fide in se reciperent & gerent. Atq; ita ad alia pro Cæsare expediunda, ab his Viennam in aulam abiit. Illic, ex senten-tia confecto negocio, reversus cum collega Stein-bergio in Frisiam anno M. CCCC. LXXXI inchoante, (ardebat quippe negocij studio) diploma secum tulit amplissimum in commo-dum ac honorem civitatis, & cum hoc fidei & mandati literas ad senatum, aliasq; item ad omnes Transslavicanas regionis ordines. In diplomate sic scriptum fuit: OSTER-GOAM VVESTERGOAMQVE, & quae cum his cohaerent trans Lavicam fl. sine con-troversia imperatoris ac imperij esse: & has, propterea quod procul dissita a sede imperatoris sint, nec ab eo absente curari bene possint, tu-multibus atq; aliys factionum malis perpetuo pre-mi atteriq;, idcirco imperatorem non precibus cuiusquam, non ulla alia re, sed solo ipsarum re-gionum commodo permotum, sponte sua, re bene consi-derata Consulibus senatuiq; Groningano op-time de rep. communi meritis, & vicinia ipsa ad rem oportunis gubernandas eas tradere, munusq; illud, quod POTESTATEM vocant, perpetuum tribuere cum omnibus, quae muneri co-haerent: & velle, ut hoc ipsum decretum suum sit constans & irrevocabile etiam apud posteros: mandare vero, ut senatus commissas hasce re-giones cum fide tueatur, regat, pacatas ser-vet: adhaec jubere quoq; VT QVI IN CON-SVLATV AVT SENATV IAM SVNT, QVIVE POST IN AVM LEGITIMB
units.tr: In the year after this one, which was 1479, Arnold Lous, whom I mentioned, came to Friesland as legate of the emperor with full authority. Having achieved nothing for which he had come, he was about to leave, and he entrusted to the Groningers the task of managing the region between the Lauwers and the Flie. He promised at the same time that if they thought he needed a larger commission and letters from the Caesar for this matter, he would obtain them himself and send them as soon as possible, without any request or reminder from them, of his own accord and eagerness. He also instructed them, by the power he held, to take on and carry out the delegated charge seriously and faithfully. Then, since he had other business to conduct for the Caesar, he went off from them to the court at Vienna. There, having brought the matter to a successful conclusion, he returned to Friesland with his colleague Steinberg at the beginning of the year 1481, for he was eager for the work. He brought with him a most ample charter for the benefit and honour of the city, and with it letters of trust and commission to the senate, and also others to all the orders of the Trans-Lauwers region. The charter was written thus: "The Oostergo and Westergo, and what belongs to them beyond the Lauwers river, are without dispute the property of the emperor and the empire. Because these lands lie far from the emperor's seat and cannot be well cared for in his absence, and are constantly oppressed and worn down by tumults and other evils of factions, the emperor, moved not by anyone's entreaties or any other cause but solely by the advantage of the regions themselves, of his own accord and after due consideration, hands over the governance of them to the consuls and senate of Groningen, who have deserved very well of the common commonwealth, and to the neighbourhood itself, which is suited to the task; and he wishes to grant, in perpetuity, that office which they call the POWER (potestas), with all that belongs to the office; and he wishes this decree of his to be firm and irrevocable even among posterity. He commands, moreover, that the senate protect, rule and keep in peace these entrusted regions faithfully; and he further orders that all who are now in the consulate or the senate, or who are afterwards legitimately elected to that order, shall be counted in the equestrian order, and that they may have the right and power to strike gold and silver coin..."

units.la: »LEGENTVR, IN EQVESTRI ORDINE OMNES CENSEANTVR: pecunia quoq; aurea argenteaq; feriunda ius & potestatem senatui eidem facere : Pro his pos ere vicissim, ex assignata hac provincia ut x millia aureorum Rhenenf. tributum quotannis sibi pendant : In hunc finem Joannem Steinbergium & Arnoldum Loum jureconsultos legatos in Frisiam jam mittere, qui cingulo equestri consules & senatores pro more induant, ac reliquis eius ordinis insignibus ornent, ornatosq; statim in possessionem potestatis istius in regionibus Trans-lavicana Frisia immittant, omnesq; earum regionum ordines jubeant, senatui huic velut imperatoris legato perpetuo, iusta ac legitima edicenti, statutaq; promulganti parere, non secus ac si ipse ea ediceret & promulgaret imperator. Poenaq; contumacib. & huic decreto obsistetib.denunciata.
units.tr: "...in return for this province, they shall pay the senate each year ten thousand Rhenish gold coins as tribute. To this end, the emperor sends now into Friesland as legates the jurists Johannes Steinberg and Arnold Lous, who shall, according to custom, invest the consuls and senators with the equestrian belt and adorn them with the other insignia of that order, and then at once put them in possession of this power in the Trans-Lauwers regions of Friesland; and they shall order all the orders of those regions to obey this senate, as the legitimate and lawful representative of the emperor, issuing and promulgating its just decrees, no less than if the emperor himself were issuing and promulgating them. And penalties are announced for the disobedient and for those who resist this decree."

units.la: Signatum diploma anno M. cccc. lxxx, die xii Calendarum Decemb. In edicto ad ordines in his regionibus, praeter oppida Doccumu, Leoardiam, Franekeram, Bolsuerdiam, Snecam, Worcumum, longus virorum praecipua nobilitatis catalogus nominatim est expressus, mandatumque omnibus, uti senatui Groniugano munus illud pro imperatore gerenti parerent, eiusq; edictis & statutis obsequerentur, gravib. propositis poenis secus facientibus. Id scriptum quatriduo post, ad diem vii Calend. Decemb. Et haec quidem monstrata senatui a legatis legendi copia facta. Sed quod pecuniam in loco negligere senatus nesciret, qui Cæsarem nimis care æstimare honorem & potestatem putaret, nec existimaret, tantum se pecuniæ ex censu regionum conficere posse, crederetq; summam in re difficultatem fore, nil horum est effectum.
units.tr: The charter was signed in the year 1480, on the twelfth day before the December Kalends. In the edict addressed to the orders in these regions, besides the towns of Dokkum, Leeuwarden, Franeker, Bolsward, Sneek and Workum, a long catalogue of the chief nobles was named by name, and it was ordered to all that they should obey the Groningen senate, which was acting in the emperor's stead in this office, and comply with its edicts and statutes, under heavy penalties for those who acted otherwise. This was written four days later, on the seventh day before the December Kalends. And indeed these things were shown to the senate by the legates, and the opportunity to read them was granted. But since the senate did not know how to ignore the money (for it thought the Caesar valued the honour and power too dearly, and did not believe that it could raise so much money from the revenues of the regions, and it believed the sum would be a great difficulty), none of these things was carried out.

units.la: Quamobrem litera fidei quidem ad senatum scripta a Cæsare in archivis reip. hujus manserunt: sed diploma cum edicto in aulam sunt a legatis relata; ubi etiam nunc inter publica imperii acta & monumenta servantur. Lous[?] de Ciflavicanis expedundum[?] negocium in se denuo recepit, atq; ita Frisia cum collega excessit. Eaq; ultima eius in rebus Frisicis mentio. Senatus abiectus hac in re animus varie acceptus a posteris, ut haud scite opportuneq; usus aula pecunia egena & cupida. Anno deinde M. cccc. LXXXII, qui Loi discessum proxime secutus est, Octobris mense WESTERGOI frequentes seditionum ac bellorum civilium formidine in hanc sententiam cum Groninganis pepigere: Ne VVestergoi impedirent eos, si qui sponte sua, sine vi in Oftergoa vellent se fœdere jungere cum Groninganis, nec eorum se rebus miscerent: Groningani contra nullos invitos subfœdus suum traherent, aut reb. novis illic studerent: VVestergoæ etiam rebus abstinerent: ordinibus his sociis injurii non essent: pax coleretur integra & perpetua. Sed ut unda maris sine fluctu, ita populus exlex & ἀναρχῷ[?] sine motu & turbis esse non potest. Itaq; tumultus minores in Oftergoa primum, deinde maiores in Westergoa omnia rursum miscuerunt. Inter quos
units.tr: For this reason, the letter of trust written by the Caesar to the senate remained in the archives of this commonwealth, but the charter together with the edict were carried back to the court by the legates, where even now they are kept among the public acts and records of the empire. Lous[?] took upon himself again the business of the Translavicans to be settled, and so he left Friesland with his colleague. And that was his last mention in Frisian affairs. The senate's spirit, dejected in this matter, was variously judged by posterity, as if it had used the court unwisely and opportunely, being needy of money and greedy for it. Then in the year 1482, which closely followed Lous's departure, in the month of October, the Westergo, in frequent fear of civil strife and wars, agreed with the Groningers on this terms: that the Westergo would not hinder those of the Oostergo who of their own accord and without force wished to join themselves in alliance with the Groningers, nor would they meddle in their affairs; the Groningers, on the other hand, would not drag any unwilling persons into their alliance, nor pursue new schemes there; the Westergo too would abstain from affairs; they would not wrong these allied orders; and peace would be kept whole and perpetual. But as the waves of the sea cannot be without foam, so a people without law and without a ruler cannot be without motion and disorder. And so the lesser tumults first in the Oostergo, then the greater ones in the Westergo, again threw everything into confusion. Among these,

units.la: SMALINGANI, ut quietos se ac tutos sisterent, anno M. CCCC. LXXXVII fœdus suum, quod cum civitate Groningana habebant, ampliatum auctumq; renovarunt. Imprimis addidêre iam de prætore ac iudicibus arbitrio Groningensium eligendis quotannis, deque compellendis iisdem ad faciendum officium per Hovetmannos, & de prætorio Hovetmannorum imperio in eum agrum: de arce, si res posceret, illic extruenda, & præfecto Groningano ei imponendo, de ferendis mutuo auxiliis contra contumaces, & domesticos peregrinosque hostes, ex Vpsterano fœdere ad verbum descripta.
units.tr: The SMALLINGERS, so that they might present themselves as quiet and safe, in the year 1487 renewed their covenant, which they had with the city of Groningen, enlarged and increased. Above all they added that the praetor and judges should henceforth be chosen each year at the discretion of the Groningers, and that they should be compelled to perform their duty by the Hovetmen, and about the praetorian rule of the Hovetmen over that territory; about a citadel, if the matter required it, to be built there, and a Groningen prefect to be placed over it; about bringing mutual aid against the contumacious, and against domestic and foreign enemies, the agreement being copied word for word from the covenant of Uppsala.

units.la: Quadriennio post, anno nimirum M. CCCC. XCI, cum rei p. mala crebresc erent, & validiora indies fierent, nil pene cuiquam tuti esset factionum exitialium causa, tandem DOCCVMANI cum DONGERANIS, & maxima OSTERGOA parte supplices facti Groningani sunt, & humillimis æque ac pertinacissimis precibus vix demum ab ijs impetrarunt, ut fœdus se cum percuterent. Id percussum est in annos XVIII, signatum die XV Calend. Octobrium.
units.tr: Four years later, namely in the year 1491, when the evils of the commonwealth were increasing and grew stronger by the day, so that scarcely anyone was safe because of ruinous factions, at last the people of Dokkum together with the Dongeradeel and the greater part of the Oostergo made suppliant appeals to the Groningers, and with the most humble and no less stubborn prayers they at length obtained from them that they should make a covenant. It was struck for eighteen years and signed on the fifteenth day before the October Kalends.

units.la: Pericriptum in eo de pace tenenda, de maleficiis severe puniendis, de auxiliis mutuo ferendis; adhæc, cæteris iudicibus in officio cesantibus Groninganis ut liceret criminis reum delatum abducere ad poenam: cui rei si quis vellet impedimento esse, centum scutatos numos reip. penderet: ut si pax diffidentibus indicenda esset propositæ poena maiore L scutatis, indiceretur à Groninganis, pœnaque in eorum usum cederet: ut à judicibus Oftergois appellatio esset ad civitatem Groninganam intra diem decimum, déque appellatione cognitio ac judicium esset conventus publici omnium socio- rum in urbe Groninga: conventus huiusmodi bis quotannis ibidem agerentur, iisque assi- derent aut praesiderent Hovetmanni oppida- ni: & hi, licet reliqui, qui adesse debebant, non adesssent omnes, tamen cum iis qui ades- sent, iudicia exercerent: reorum multas & contumaciae poenas more suo per praetorias literas Groninganis exigere ab Oftergois licere- ret: caedíu multas dimidias civitas haberet, per mandata praetoria exactas sola in aerarium suum verteret: denique Hovetmannis Gro- ninganis ius esset iudices Oftergoos cesantes in officio, ad faciendum officium compellere.
units.tr: In it was written down a concern for keeping the peace, for punishing crimes severely, for bringing mutual aid; further, that when the other judges in the Oostergo were negligent in their office, the Groningers might be permitted to carry off an accused criminal to punishment; that if anyone wished to be an obstacle to this, he should pay the republic one hundred gold shields; that if peace had to be declared against those who defied it, under a penalty larger than fifty shields, it should be declared by the Groningers, and the penalty should accrue to their use; that appeal from the Oostergo judges should lie to the city of Groningen within ten days, and that the hearing and judgment of appeals should belong to a public assembly of all the allies in the city of Groningen; such assemblies were to be held there twice a year, and the Hovetmen of the towns were to attend or preside over them; and although the rest who ought to be present were not all present, yet the judgments should be carried out with those who were present; that the Groningers should be permitted to exact from the Oostergo the fines of the accused and the penalties for contumacy in their own manner, by praetorian letters; that the city should have half the fines of the cases, collected by praetorian mandates, and should turn them solely into its own treasury; and finally that the Groningen Hovetmen should have the right to compel the Oostergo judges who were negligent in their office to perform their duty.

units.la: Subscripsere foederi, primum senatus populusq; DOCCVMANVS, antistites coenobiorum sex, & magnus nobilium virorum munerus, praeter vicos & vicanos plurimos; dein plures se paulatim associarunt, demum universa OSTERGOA, exceptis, quos factionum studium in diversa agebat, est adscripta: unde foedus OSTERGOVM vulgo nuncupatum fuit. Anno posteró M. CCCC. XCI, cum tumultus huius foederis gratia extitissent, autore potissimum & concitatore Tiardo Moccama, totáq; Scriringiorum factio in Westergoa se commoveret, LEOARDII a vi factionis sibi metuentes, ut se magis magisq; firmarent, speciali se sedere & arctiore cum Groninninganis junxerunt. Hoc foedere promiscere SENIOR, SCABINI, SENATVS RELIQVVS, ET XIIIVIRI totius populi nomine, fideles se socios Groningensium futuros in annos XXIIII ex formula foederis Doccumani, eiusque foederis conditiones omnes servaturos: praeterea permissuros, ut » lites civium suorum cum civibus, de quibus » appellare superiores judices placet, à SE-» NATV GRONINGANO, temporibus in foedere Doccumano expressis, RECOGNOSCENTVR: caeterae lites aut civium cum peregrinis, aut peregrinorum cum ijsdem peregrinis, id est, ijs qui Leoardiae domicilium non habent, ab Hovetmannis Groningensibus, & conventu juridico sociorum, ut est in eodem foedere Doccumano, definiantur.
units.tr: The first to subscribe to the covenant were the senate and people of Dokkum, the abbots of six monasteries, and a great number of the noble men, apart from the villages and very many villagers; then more joined themselves gradually, and at last the whole of the Oostergo, except those whom the zeal of factions drove in different directions, was enrolled; whence the covenant was commonly called the Oostergo covenant. In the following year, 1491, when tumults had arisen on account of this covenant, chiefly through the instigation and agitation of Tiard Moccama, and the whole faction of the Scriringers stirred itself in Westergo, the people of Leeuwarden, fearing violence from the faction, so that they might strengthen themselves more and more, joined themselves in a special and closer bond with the Groningers. In this covenant the elder, the aldermen, the remaining senate and the Thirteen promised, in the name of the whole people, that they would be faithful allies of the Groningers for twenty-four years, according to the form of the Dokkum covenant, and would keep all the conditions of that covenant; moreover, they would permit that suits between their citizens and citizens about whom it pleases to appeal to the higher judges should be examined by the GRONINGEN SENATE, within the times expressed in the Dokkum covenant; other suits, either of citizens with foreigners or of foreigners with the same foreigners, that is, with those who do not have a domicile at Leeuwarden, should be decided by the Groningen Hovetmen and the juridical assembly of the allies, as is set out in that same Dokkum covenant.

units.la: » Dein additum, VT GRONINGANI » PRÆFECTVM DENT LEOARDIANIS, » qui vel in oppido, vel in eius vicinia commo-» do loco sedem habeat; isq; scabini aut senio-» ris locum teneat in senatu oppidano eaq; po-» testate sit, qua ipse, si adsit, SENATVS GRO-» NINGANVS, cujus vicem geret: eidemque praefecto Leoardiani stipendium solvant de-cennio proximo aureos Rhenanos centenos annuos: interea socii rationem ineant aliam stipendij ejusdem conficiendi, quae duret ad foederis usq; finem, sintq; Leoardiani ab onere illo centenorum aureorum deinceps liberi.
units.tr: Then it was added that the Groningers should give the Leeuwardeners a prefect, who should have a seat in a convenient place in the town or its neighbourhood; he should hold the place of an alderman or senior member in the town senate, and have the same power as the Groningen Senate itself, if it were present, whose deputy he would be. The Leeuwardeners were to pay this same prefect a hundred Rhenish gold coins a year for the next ten years; meanwhile the allies were to devise another way of raising this salary, which should last until the end of the covenant, and after that the Leeuwardeners would be free of the burden of those hundred gold coins.

units.la: Praefectum hunc si quis ausu temerario occidat, prehensus capite poenas vicissim pendat, fuga elapsus omnibus bonis mobilibus & immobilibus exuatur, eaq; ad arbitrium senatus in fiscum redigantur Groningenfium: eædem vero eẽm fi satelles aut minister jussu alterius patret, & ipse & qui jufit, eadem teneantur noxa,idemq; supplicium pendant: At fi vulnere eundem quis leferit, poenam vulnerati hominis nobilis duplam solvat. Cetera sunt de obsidibus sex arbitrio Groningenfiu legendis, & in custodia habedis,sicubi cotingat fœderis hujus observatione Leoardienfiu vitio claudicare. Signatiu celebratu, Leoardia die VI Idui Octobr. Eodemq, tempore magno numero viri nobiles primarum familiarium, qui baptenus foederi Oftergoo fe opposuerant tam Weftergoi quam Oftergoi,item, oppida Franekera & Worcumii, cum coharentib: praefecturis, cum audijfent Groninganos jam Leoardiam ingressos, Leoardiofq, fœderis feriundi cum his peravidos esse, ipsi quoq, re bene deliberata, dimisso armorum consilio, cum Groninganis pepigere in hunc modum: Ne fas effet ipsis, turbare Groningenses, & fœdus cum iis jam habentes, aut impofterum habituros: nec contra Groninganus liceret miscere fe rebus illorum, aut illos illorumq; subditos, aut regiones illis invitis sub fœdus suum trahere: quod fi compertum fuerit eorum aliquem in Groninganos, aut horum fo-cios aliquid deliquisse, de eo ad arbitrium quatuor virorum, duorum e Senatu Groninganos, duorum ex ipsis datorum satisfaciat.
units.tr: If anyone should rashly kill this prefect, when caught he is to pay the penalty in turn; if he escapes by flight, he is to be stripped of all his movable and immovable goods, and these are to be confiscated to the treasury of the Groningers at the discretion of the senate. If a servant or minister of the prefect does the deed on another's orders, both he and the one who gave the order are to be held to the same liability and pay the same punishment. But if someone wounds the prefect, he is to pay double the penalty for wounding a noble man. The rest concerns six hostages, to be chosen at the discretion of the Groningers and held in custody, should the Leeuwardeners at any point fail in the observance of this covenant. Signed and celebrated at Leeuwarden, on the 10th of October. At the same time, a great number of noblemen of the chief families, who had hitherto opposed the covenant with the Ostergo, both of the Westergo and the Ostergo, likewise the towns of Franeker and Workum, together with their attached prefectures, when they heard that the Groningers had now entered Leeuwarden and were eager to make a covenant with them there, themselves too, after considering the matter carefully, gave up their plan of arms and agreed terms with the Groningers in this manner: that it should not be lawful for them to disturb the Groningers, and to have or in future to have a covenant with them; nor should it be lawful for the Groningers to meddle in their affairs, or to draw them or their subjects, or their regions, under their covenant against their will. If it should be discovered that any of them had wronged the Groningers or their allies, he is to make satisfaction for it at the discretion of four men, two from the Groningen Senate and two given by the others themselves.

units.la: Nec multos post dies Snecani, Slotenses, Istani ceteriq, horum socij factionis Scirin- qui fœderis hostes insigni clade ad Barra-bufium a foederatis correpti cum Bocconb HARINGÆO factionis principe, ad arbitrium victorum conditiones accepere. Iurarunt, fœ-deri Oftergoo non se semet oppositurus, nec impedimento iis futuros, si qui deinceps aut Oftergoi aut VVestergoi accedere eidem velent: nullum jus imperiumve in universam Oftergoam, aut ullam eius partem sibi arro-gaturos, ablata redditurosque in integrum restituturos, controversiam cum Galamæis arbitrio Groningensium submissuros: Groningen-genses in persequendis iniuriis contra VVestergoos hac pactione non comprehensos non impedituros: è sociis in has leges peccanti nemini patrocinaturos: detrimenta, impen-dia, molestias belli Groningani & Oftergois XVII millib. aureorum Rhenens. & quingentis spacio 1x mensium terminis pensionibus farturos. Deniq; alia obligandæ fidei vincula gravia & asperæ adjuncta: quæ in historia ex-pono. Tum consternatis totius factionis ad-versæ animis, quotquot eius in Oftergoa supe-rerant, viri nobiles, quos hactenus pertinacia siverat[?] accedere, eidem fœderi Oftergoo accesserunt.
units.tr: Not many days later, the Snecanians, Slotenses, Istanians and the others of their faction, who were enemies of the covenant, were struck by a notable defeat at Baarderadeel by the confederates, together with Bocco Haringa, the leader of the faction, and accepted terms at the discretion of the victors. They swore that they would not oppose the covenant with the Ostergo, nor would they be an obstacle to those who might afterwards wish to join it, whether Ostergoers or Westergoers; that they would claim no right or rule over the whole of the Ostergo or any part of it; that they would restore what had been taken and make full restitution; that they would submit their dispute with the Galamians to the arbitration of the Groningers; that the Groningers would not be hindered in pursuing injuries against the Westergoers not included in this agreement; that none of the allies would defend anyone who offended against these laws; and that they would pay the losses, expenses and troubles of the war to the Groningers and the Ostergoers, 17,000 Rhenish gold coins, and 500 more, in instalments over nine months. Finally, other heavy bonds of obligation and harsh conditions were added, which I set out in the history. Then, with the minds of the whole hostile faction dismayed, all those noblemen of the Ostergo who had hitherto been held back by obstinacy, joined that same covenant with the Ostergo.

units.la: In hoc rerum statu, cum omnia ad amplian-dos fœderis huiusce fines spectare viderentur, venit in Frisiam legatus Cæsaris Friderici OTTO LANGIUS canonicus Moguntinus, ut Frisiorum dissidia componeret. Cuius adventu respi-rantes Scaringi (horum enim precibus data legati missio erat) animos rursum extulere, tur-basq; dedere fœderatis. Nec multo post è vita decessit Fridericus III imperator, ad quem reverterat. verterat legatus, catera ad pacandam Frisiam, uti firebat[?], procuraturus. Idem vero anno sequente, nomine MAXIMILIANI regis, qui patri successerat, in Frisiam rediit, mandata secum ferens de EPHORO in Frisia, quem PO-TESTATEM dicere mos erat, designando, & simul diploma de libertate gentis. Sed & civitas Groningana, quae suos quoq; homines una cum socijs delegaverat ad eundem regem, amplissimum diploma ab eo impetravit, quo foedus OS-TERGOUM utraq; parte petente solenniter confirmatum fuit, praesentib. in aula, & nequicq; contra nitentibus Scringijs. Id diploma datum Campoduni die xxiii Maii: eoq; comprehensi quod illi, qui post percussum foedus primum eidem deinde accesserant. Ait litera regis Camstraeo[?] data viro nobili, in aula nato, regiq; grato, differentionem peperere: dissensio tumultus dedit: per eos iste deducta res est, ut BOLSVERDIA, VVORCVMVM, STAVERA, HINDELOPA, & maxima nobilitatis VVESTERGOÆ, maxima item plebis rustica pars foedus novum cum Gro-ninganis, foederi OSTERGOO simillimum, percusserint, deniq; paulo post tota pene VVESTERGOA excepta FRANEKERA cum coniuratis viris nobilibus, in Groningensium ac sociorum potestatem venerit: quod factum anno Christi M. CCCC. XCVI.
units.tr: In this state of affairs, when everything seemed to aim at enlarging the bounds of this covenant, the legate of the Emperor Frederick, Otto Langius, canon of Mainz, came into Frisia to settle the quarrels of the Frisians. At his arrival the Scarlingers (for it was at their prayers that the legate had been sent) took fresh heart and again raised their spirits and gave trouble to the confederates. Not long after, Emperor Frederick III died, to whom the legate had returned, and the legate was to take charge of the rest for pacifying Frisia, as he was urged to do. In the following year, however, in the name of King Maximilian, who had succeeded his father, he returned to Frisia, carrying with him instructions about appointing a steward in Frisia, whom it was customary to call the Governor, and at the same time a charter concerning the freedom of the people. But the city of Groningen, which had also delegated its own men together with the allies to the same king, obtained from him a very ample charter by which the covenant with the Ostergo was solemnly confirmed at the request of both parties, the Scarlingers being present at court and struggling in vain against it. This charter was given at Kampen on the 23rd of May; and by it were secured those who, after the covenant was struck, had first joined it and then later joined it. A letter of the king, given at Cambrai to a nobleman, born at court and pleasing to the king, caused disagreement; dissension gave rise to tumult; through those men this matter was brought about, so that Bolsward, Workum, Staveren, Hindeloopen, and the greatest part of the nobility of the Westergo, and likewise the greatest part of the rustic common people, struck a new covenant with the Groningers, very like the covenant with the Ostergo; and finally, a little after, almost all of the Westergo, except Franeker, together with the conspiring noblemen, came into the power of the Groningers and their allies; which was done in the year of Christ 1496.

units.la: Hoc tempore MAXIMILIANVS rex cum ALBERTO SAXONIÆ ducé comparat de Frisia subigenda : e[?]Albertus velut Sciringÿs[?] auxilio futurus militem in Frisiam mittit : Ei mox alium, dissimulato nomine & consilio suo, submittit Vetcopero- rum, stipendia facturum, ut regionem atte-rerent, & enervem redderent. Tum cum maturum videretur, fessis[?] penè omnibus diploma in Frisiam missum, quo Frisiae gubernatio e[?]Al-berto Saxoni sub Potestatis titulo à e[?]Maximi-liano, & ordinibus imperij assignabatur, eaq; ju- bebatur esse perpetua, transfitura in hæredes. Ad-ditum tamen, ut belli impendijs refusis, & certâ pecunię summa soluta, à Philippo Burgundo e[?]Maximiliani filio, gubernatio tota & omne in Frisiam jus ad eundem transfiret. e[?]Albertus per suos, quos præmiserat, oppressis omnib.
